Having done the preliminary work with sense-sphere consciousness, he then made a determination with fine-material-sphere consciousness, creating an image like the moon's disc rising from the enclosure of the eastern Yugandhara mountain, breaking through and emerging.

Devasaṅgho taṃ disvā – “aññopi nu kho, bho, cando uggato”ti āha. Atha candaṃ ohāya āsannatare jāte “na cando, sūriyo uggato”ti, puna āsannatare jāte “na sūriyo, devavimānaṃ eka”nti, puna āsannatare jāte “na devavimānaṃ, devaputto eko”ti, puna āsannatare jāte “na devaputto, mahābrahmā eko”ti, puna āsannatare jāte “na mahābrahmā, aparopi bho buddho āgato”ti āha. Tattha puthujjanadevatā cintayiṃsu – “ekabuddhassa tāva ayaṃ devatāsannipāto, dvinnaṃ kīva mahanto bhavissatī”ti. Ariyadevatā cintayiṃsu – “ekissā lokadhātuyā dve buddhā nāma natthi, addhā bhagavatā attanā sadiso añño eko buddho nimmito”ti.

Seeing him, the assembly of devas said, "Has another moon arisen, sirs?" Then, as he drew nearer, leaving the moon aside, they said, "It is not the moon, the sun has arisen!" As he came even closer, they said, "It is not the sun, it is a deva mansion." Drawing nearer still, they said, "It is not a deva mansion, it is a single deva." Coming closer yet, they said, "It is not a deva, it is a Great Brahmā." And when he was very near, they said, "It is not a Great Brahmā, another Buddha has come, sirs!" There, the ordinary devas thought, "For one Buddha there is this assembly of devas; how much greater will it be for two?" The noble devas reflected, "In one world-sphere there are not two Buddhas. Surely the Blessed One has created another Buddha similar to himself."

Atha tassa devasaṅghassa passantasseva nimmitabuddho āgantvā dasabalaṃ avanditvāva sammukhaṭṭhāne samasamaṃ katvā māpite āsane nisīdi. Bhagavatopi dvattiṃsa mahāpurisalakkhaṇāni, nimmitassāpi dvattiṃsāva, bhagavatopi [M 2.0277] sarīrā chabbaṇṇarasmiyo nikkhamanti[V 2.0248], nimmitassāpi, bhagavato sarīrarasmiyo nimmitassa sarīre paṭihaññanti, nimmitassa sarīrarasmiyo bhagavato kāye paṭihaññanti. Tā dvinnampi buddhānaṃ sarīrato [P 2.0684] uggamma akaniṭṭhabhavanaṃ āhacca tato paṭinivattitvā devatānaṃ matthakapariyante otaritvā cakkavāḷamukhavaṭṭiyaṃ patiṭṭhahiṃsu. Sakalacakkavāḷagabbhaṃ suvaṇṇamayavaṅkagopānasīvinaddhamiva cetiyagharaṃ virocittha. Dasasahassacakkavāḷadevatā ekacakkavāḷe rāsibhūtā dvinnaṃ buddhānaṃ rasmigabbhantaraṃ pavisitvā aṭṭhaṃsu. Nimmitabuddho nisīdantoyeva dasabalassa bodhipallaṅke kilesappahānaṃ abhitthavanto –

Then, as that assembly of devas looked on, the created Buddha came and, without paying homage to the Ten-Powered One, sat down on a created seat made equal to his and placed directly in front of him. The Blessed One had the thirty-two marks of a Great Man, and the created one also had thirty-two. From the Blessed One’s body, six-hued rays emanated, and from the created one’s as well. The rays from the Blessed One’s body struck the created one’s body, and the rays from the created one’s body struck the Blessed One’s body. Rising from the bodies of both Buddhas, those rays struck the Akaniṭṭha realm and then, turning back, descended upon the crowns of the devas before settling on the rim of the world-sphere. The entire interior of the world-sphere shone like a reliquary chamber interwoven with curved golden rafters. Devas from ten thousand world-spheres, massed together in a single world-sphere, entered the space within the rays of the two Buddhas and stood there. As he sat, the created Buddha began extolling the Ten-Powered One's abandonment of defilements at the Bodhi-throne:

“Pucchāmi muniṃ pahūtapaññaṃ,

Tiṇṇaṃ pāraṅgataṃ parinibbutaṃ ṭhitattaṃ;

Nikkhamma gharā panujja kāme,

Kathaṃ bhikkhu sammā so loke paribbajeyyā”ti. (su. ni. 361) –

"I ask the sage of abundant wisdom, who has crossed over, reached the far shore, is fully extinguished, and steadfast in mind; having gone forth from home, having driven out sensual pleasures, how should that monk wander rightly in the world?"

Gāthaṃ abhāsi. Satthā devatānaṃ tāva cittakallatājananatthaṃ āgatāgatānaṃ nāmagottāni kathessāmīti cintetvā ācikkhissāmi, bhikkhavetiādimāha.

He spoke the verse. The Teacher, thinking, 'First, I will declare the names and clans of the devas who have come, in order to make their minds receptive,' said, 'I will explain, monks,' and so forth.

334. Tattha silokamanukassāmīti akkharapadaniyamitaṃ vacanasaṅghātaṃ pavattayissāmi. Yattha bhummā tadassitāti yesu yesu ṭhānesu bhummā devatā taṃ taṃ nissitā. Ye sitā girigabbharantiādīhi tesaṃ bhikkhūnaṃ vaṇṇaṃ kathesi, ye bhikkhū girikucchiṃ nissitāti attho. Pahitattāti pesitacittā. Samāhitāti avikkhittā.

334. Herein, 'I will recite a verse' means: I will utter a collection of speech defined by letters and words. 'Where the earth-devas are, there they are based' means: in whatever places the earth-devas are, they are dependent on that place. By 'Those who are in mountain caves,' and so on, it refers to those monks; the meaning is 'monks who rely on a mountain cavern.' 'With determined minds' means with minds sent forth. 'Composed' means undistracted.

Puthūti bahujanā. Sīhāva sallīnāti sīhā viya nilīnā ekattaṃ upagatā. Lomahaṃsābhisambhunoti lomahaṃsaṃ abhibhavitvā ṭhitā, nibbhayāti vuttaṃ hoti. Odātamanasā suddhāti odātacittā hutvā suddhā. Vippasannāmanāvilāti vippasannaanāvilā.

'Many' means numerous people. 'Like lions, secluded' means like lions they are withdrawn, having attained solitude. 'Overcoming what makes the hair stand on end' means having overcome what makes the hair stand on end, they stand firm; that is to say, they are fearless. 'With pure minds, purified' means having become pure-minded, they are purified. 'Serene and limpid minds' means serene and unclouded.

Bhiyyopañcasate ñatvāti sammāsambuddhena saddhiṃ atirekapañcasate bhikkhū jānitvā. Vane kāpilavatthaveti kapilavatthusamīpamhi jāte vanasaṇḍe. Tato āmantayī satthāti tadā āmantayi. Sāvake [M 2.0278] sāsane rateti attano dhammadesanāya savanante jātattā sāvake [P 2.0685] sikkhattayasāsane [V 2.0249] ratattā sāsane rate. Idaṃ sabbaṃ – “silokamanukassāmī”ti vacanato aññena vuttaṃ viya katvā vadati.

'Having known the more than five hundred' means: having known the over five hundred monks, together with the Perfectly Enlightened One. 'In the wood of Kapilavatthu' means: in the forest grove that arose near Kapilavatthu. 'Then the Teacher addressed' means: at that time he addressed them. 'Disciples delighting in the Teaching' means: they are 'disciples' (sāvake) because they were born at the end of hearing his Dhamma discourse, and they 'delight in the Teaching' (sāsane rate) because they delight in the teaching of the threefold training. He speaks all this as if it were said by another, on account of his statement, 'I will recite a verse'.

Devakāyā abhikkantā, te vijānātha bhikkhavoti te dibbacakkhunā vijānāthāti nesaṃ bhikkhūnaṃ dibbacakkhuñāṇābhinīhāratthāya kathesi. Te ca ātappamakaruṃ, sutvā buddhassa sāsananti te ca bhikkhū taṃ buddhasāsanaṃ sutvā tāvadeva tadatthāya vīriyaṃ kariṃsu.

'The hosts of devas have approached; discern them, monks.' He said this for the purpose of directing the minds of those monks to the knowledge of the divine eye, meaning, 'Discern them with the divine eye.' 'And they made an effort, having heard the Buddha's teaching' means: and those monks, having heard that teaching of the Buddha, immediately made an effort for that purpose.

Evaṃ katamattātappānaṃyeva tesaṃ pāturahu ñāṇaṃ. Kīdisaṃ? Amanussānaṃ dassanaṃ dibbacakkhuñāṇaṃ uppajji. Na taṃ tehi tasmiṃ khaṇe parikammaṃ katvā uppāditaṃ. Ariyamaggeneva hi taṃ nipphannaṃ. Amanussadassanatthaṃ panassa abhinīhāramattameva kataṃ. Satthāpi – “atthi tumhākaṃ ñāṇaṃ, taṃ nīharitvā tena hi te vijānāthā”ti idameva sandhāya “te vijānātha, bhikkhavo”ti āha.

Thus, for those who had just made the effort, knowledge manifested. What kind? The knowledge of the divine eye for the seeing of non-humans arose. It was not produced by them at that moment by performing preliminary work, for it had already been accomplished together with the noble path. For the purpose of seeing non-humans, however, only the directing of the mind was done. The Teacher also, referring to just this, said, 'You have the knowledge; having brought it forth, discern them with it, monks.'

Appeke satamaddakkhunti tesu bhikkhūsu ekacce bhikkhū amanussānaṃ sataṃ addasaṃsu. Sahassaṃ atha sattarinti eke sahassaṃ. Eke sattati sahassāni.

'Some saw a hundred' means: among those monks, some monks saw a hundred non-humans. 'A thousand, then seventy' means: some saw a thousand, and some saw seventy thousand.

Sataṃ eke sahassānanti eke satasahassaṃ addasaṃsu. Appekenantamaddakkhunti vipulaṃ addasaṃsu, satavasena sahassavasena ca aparicchinnepi addasaṃsūti attho. Kasmā? Yasmā disā sabbā phuṭā ahuṃ, bharitā sampuṇṇāva ahesuṃ.

'Some, a hundred thousand' means: some saw a hundred thousand. 'Some saw a countless number' means: they saw a vast number; that is, they saw them unquantifiable by way of hundreds and thousands. Why? Because all directions were pervaded; they were filled, indeed completely full.

Tañca sabbaṃ abhiññāyāti yaṃ tesu ekenekena diṭṭhaṃ, tañca sabbaṃ jānitvā. Vavatthitvāna cakkhumāti hatthatale lekhaṃ viya paccakkhato vavatthapetvā pañcahi cakkhūhi cakkhumā satthā. Tato āmantayīti pubbe vuttagāthameva nāmagottakittanatthāya āha. Tumhe ete vijānātha, passatha, oloketha, ye vohaṃ kittayissāmīti ayamettha sambandho. Girāhīti vacanehi. Anupubbasoti anupaṭipāṭiyā.

Tañca sabbaṃ abhiññāya means: having fully known all that which was seen by each one of them. Vavatthitvāna cakkhumā means: the Teacher, the one with vision, having determined it directly, like a line on the palm of the hand, with the five eyes. Tato āmantayī means: he spoke the previously uttered verse for the purpose of declaring their names and clans. "You should know these, see them, behold them, whom I shall proclaim to you"—this is the connection here. Girāhi means: by words. Anupubbaso means: sequentially.

335. Sattasahassā te yakkhā, bhummā kāpilavatthavāti sattasahassā tāvettha kapilavatthuṃ nissāya nibbattā bhummā yakkhāyevāti vadati[M 2.0279]. Iddhimantoti [P 2.0686] dibbaiddhiyuttā. Jutimantoti ānubhāvasampannā. Vaṇṇavantoti sarīravaṇṇasampannā. Yasassinoti parivārasampannā. Modamānā abhikkāmunti tuṭṭhacittā āgatā. Bhikkhūnaṃ samitiṃ vananti imaṃ mahāvanaṃ bhikkhūnaṃ santikaṃ bhikkhūnaṃ [V 2.0250] dassanatthāya āgatā. Atha vā samitinti samūhaṃ, bhikkhusamūhaṃ dassanāya āgatātipi attho.

335. Sattasahassā te yakkhā, bhummā kāpilavatthavā means: here, he says, are seven thousand yakkhas, earth-deities native to Kapilavatthu, born dependent on it. Iddhimanto means: endowed with divine psychic power. Jutimanto means: possessed of majesty. Vaṇṇavanto means: endowed with beautiful complexion. Yasassino means: possessed of a retinue. Modamānā abhikkāmunti means: they came with joyful minds. Bhikkhūnaṃ samitiṃ vanaṃ means: they came to this great forest, into the presence of the monks, for the purpose of seeing the monks. Alternatively, samitiṃ means assembly; they came to see the assembly of monks—this is also the meaning.

Chasahassā hemavatā, yakkhā nānattavaṇṇinoti chasahassā hemavatapabbate nibbattayakkhā, te ca sabbepi nīlādivaṇṇavasena nānattavaṇṇā.

Chasahassā hemavatā, yakkhā nānattavaṇṇino means: six thousand yakkhas born on Mount Hemavata; and all of them are of various colors, such as blue and so forth.

Sātāgirā tisahassāti sātāgiripabbate nibbattayakkhā tisahassā.

Sātāgirā tisahassā means: three thousand yakkhas born on Mount Sātāgiri.

Iccete soḷasasahassāti ete sabbepi soḷasasahassā honti.

Iccete soḷasasahassā means: thus, these are sixteen thousand in all.

Vessāmittā pañcasatāti vessāmittapabbate nibbattā pañcasatā.

Vessāmittā pañcasatā means: five hundred born on Mount Vessāmitta.

Kumbhīro rājagahikoti rājagahanagare nibbatto kumbhīro nāma yakkho. Vepullassa nivesananti tassa vepullapabbato nivesanaṃ nivāsanaṭṭhānanti attho. Bhiyyo naṃ satasahassaṃ, yakkhānaṃ payirupāsatīti taṃ atirekaṃ yakkhānaṃ satasahassaṃ payirupāsati. Kumbhīro rājagahiko, sopāgā samitiṃ vananti sopi kumbhīro saparivāro imaṃ vanaṃ bhikkhusamitiṃ dassanatthāya āgato.

Kumbhīro rājagahiko means: the yakkha named Kumbhīra, native to Rājagaha. Vepullassa nivesanaṃ means: Mount Vepulla is his abode, that is, his dwelling place. Bhiyyo naṃ satasahassaṃ, yakkhānaṃ payirupāsati means: more than a hundred thousand yakkhas attend upon him. Kumbhīro rājagahiko, sopāgā samitiṃ vanaṃ means: that Kumbhīra of Rājagaha also came with his retinue to this forest for the purpose of seeing the assembly of monks.

336. Purimañca disaṃ rājā, dhataraṭṭho pasāsatīti pācīnadisaṃ anusāsati. Gandhabbānaṃ adhipatīti catūsupi disāsu gandhabbānaṃ jeṭṭhako. Sabbe te tassa vase vattanti. Mahārājā yasassisoti mahāparivāro eso mahārājā.

336. Purimañca disaṃ rājā, dhataraṭṭho pasāsati means: he governs the eastern quarter. Gandhabbānaṃ adhipatī means: he is the chief of the gandhabbas in all four directions. All of them are under his power. Mahārājā yasassī means: this great king has a large retinue.

Puttāpi [M 2.0280] tassa bahavo, indanāmā mahabbalāti tassa dhataraṭṭhassa bahavo mahabbalā puttā, te sabbe sakkassa devarañño nāmadhārakā.

Puttāpi tassa bahavo, indanāmā mahabbalā means: that Dhataraṭṭha has many sons of great strength, and all of them bear the name of Sakka, the king of the devas.

Virūḷho taṃ pasāsatīti taṃ disaṃ virūḷho anusāsati.

Virūḷho taṃ pasāsati means: Virūḷha governs that direction.

Puttāpi tassāti tassāpi tādisāyeva puttā. Pāḷiyaṃ pana “mahabbalā”ti likhanti. Aṭṭhakathāyaṃ sabbavāresu “mahābalā”ti pāṭho.

Puttāpi tassā means: his sons, too, are of the same kind. In the Pāli text, however, they write ‘mahabbalā’. In the commentary, in all instances, the reading is ‘mahābalā’.

“Purimaṃ [P 2.0687][V 2.0251] disaṃ dhataraṭṭho, dakkhiṇena virūḷhako;

Pacchimena virūpakkho, kuvero uttaraṃ disaṃ.

"Dhataraṭṭha in the eastern direction, Virūḷhaka in the southern; Virūpakkha in the western, Kuvera in the northern direction.

Cattāro te mahārājā, samantā caturo disā;

Daddallamānā aṭṭhaṃsu, vane kāpilavatthave”ti.

Those four great kings stood resplendent, surrounding the four directions in the forest of Kapilavatthu."

Imā pana gāthā sabbasaṅgāhikavasena vuttā.

These verses, however, were spoken in a comprehensive manner.

Ayañcettha attho – dasasahassacakkavāḷe dhataraṭṭhā nāma mahārājāno atthi. Te sabbepi koṭisatasahassakoṭisatasahassagandhabbaparivārā āgantvā puratthimāya disāya kapilavatthumahāvanato paṭṭhāya cakkavāḷagabbhaṃ pūretvā ṭhitā. Evaṃ dakkhiṇadisādīsu virūḷhakādayo. Tenevāha – “samantā caturo disā, daddallamānā aṭṭhaṃsū”ti. Idañhi vuttaṃ hoti – “samantā cakkavāḷehi āgantvā caturo disā pabbatamatthakesu aggikkhandhā viya suṭṭhu jalamānā ṭhitā”ti. Te pana yasmā kapilavatthuvanameva sandhāya āgatā, tasmā cakkavāḷaṃ pūretvā cakkavāḷena samasamā ṭhitāpi – “vane kāpilavatthave”ti vuttā.

And this is the meaning here: in the ten-thousandfold world-system, there are great kings named Dhataraṭṭha. All of them, with retinues of countless gandhabbas, came and stood, filling the interior of the world-system, starting from the Great Forest of Kapilavatthu in the eastern direction. Likewise in the southern direction and so on with Virūḷhaka and the others. For that reason, he said: "All around the four directions, they stood, shining brilliantly." For this is what is meant: "Having come from all the surrounding world-systems, they stood in the four directions, blazing brightly like masses of fire upon mountain peaks." However, because they came with the Great Forest of Kapilavatthu as their specific destination, they are spoken of as being "in the forest of Kapilavatthu," even though they stood filling the world-system, coextensive with the world-system.

337. Tesaṃ māyāvino dāsā, āguṃ vañcanikā saṭhāti tesaṃ mahārājānaṃ katapāpapaṭicchādanalakkhaṇāya māyāya yuttā kuṭilācārā dāsā atthi, ye sammukhaparammukhavañcanāhi lokaṃ vañcanato “vañcanikā”ti ca, kerāṭiyasāṭheyyena samannāgatattā “saṭhā”ti ca vuccanti, tepi āgatāti attho. Māyā kuṭeṇḍu viṭeṇḍu, viṭucca viṭuṭo sahāti te dāsā sabbepi māyākārakāva. Nāmena panettha eko kuṭeṇḍu nāma, eko viṭeṇḍu nāma. Pāḷiyaṃ pana “veṭeṇḍū”ti likhanti. Eko viṭucca nāma, eko viṭuṭo nāma. Sahāti sopi viṭuṭo tehi saheva āgato.

Tesaṃ māyāvino dāsā, āguṃ vañcanikā saṭhā means: those great kings have servants who are endowed with deceit, which is characterized by the concealing of evil deeds, and are of crooked conduct. Because they deceive the world through trickery both in person and behind one's back, they are called ‘vañcanikā’ (tricksters); and because they are possessed of craftiness and fraud, they are called ‘saṭhā’ (cunning). They too came—this is the meaning. Māyā kuṭeṇḍu viṭeṇḍu, viṭucca viṭuṭo sahā means: all those servants are practitioners of deceit. Here, by name, one is Kuṭeṇḍu, and one is Viṭeṇḍu. In the Pāli text, however, they write ‘Veṭeṇḍu’. One is named Viṭucca, and one is Viṭuṭo. Sahā (along with) means: that Viṭuṭo also came together with them.

Candano [M 2.0281] kāmaseṭṭho ca, kinnighaṇḍu nighaṇḍu cāti aparo kinnighaṇḍu nāma. Pāḷiyaṃ pana “kinnughaṇḍū”ti likhanti. Nighaṇḍu cāti añño nighaṇḍu nāma, ettakā dāsā. Ito pare pana –

Candano kāmaseṭṭho ca, kinnighaṇḍu nighaṇḍu ca: Another is named Kinnighaṇḍu. In the Pāli text, however, they write ‘Kinnughaṇḍu’. Nighaṇḍu ca means: and another named Nighaṇḍu. So many are the servants. But after these:

“Panādo [V 2.0252] opamañño ca, devasuto ca mātali;

Cittaseno ca gandhabbo, naḷo rājā janesabho;

Āguṃ pañcasikho ceva, timbarū sūriyavacchasā”ti. –

337. "Panāda and Opamañña, and Mātali the deva's charioteer; Cittasena the gandhabba, King Naḷa, lord of men; Pañcasikha also came, and Timbaru with Suriyavacchasā."

Ime [P 2.0688] devarājāno. Tattha devasutoti devasārathi. Cittasenoti citto ca seno ca cittaseno ca. Gandhabboti ayaṃ cittaseno gandhabbakāyiko devaputto, na kevalaṃ cesa, sabbe pete panādādayo gandhabbā eva. Naḷorājāti naḷakāradevaputto nāmeko. Janesabhoti janavasabho devaputto. Āguṃ pañcasikho cevāti pañcasikho ceva devaputto āgato. Timbarūti timbarū nāma gandhabbadevarājā. Sūriyavacchasāti tasseva dhītā.

These are the deva-kings. Therein, 'devasuta' is the deva charioteer. 'Cittasena' is Citta and Sena, and also Cittasena. 'Gandhabba' means this Cittasena is a devaputta of the gandhabba host; and not only he, but all these, beginning with Panāda, are indeed gandhabbas. 'Naḷorājā' is a certain devaputta named Naḷakāra. 'Janesabha' is the devaputta Janavasabha. 'Pañcasikha also came' means the devaputta Pañcasikha also came. 'Timbarū' is the gandhabba deva-king named Timbarū. 'Sūriyavacchasā' is his daughter.

Ete caññe ca rājāno, gandhabbā saha rājubhīti ete ca nāmavasena vuttagandhabbarājāno aññe ca etehi rājūhi saddhiṃ bahū gandhabbā. Modamānā abhikkāmuṃ, bhikkhūnaṃ samitiṃ vananti haṭṭhatuṭṭhacittā bhikkhusaṅghasamitiṃ imaṃ vanaṃ āgatāti attho.

'These and other kings, gandhabbas together with their rulers' means: these gandhabba kings mentioned by name, and many other gandhabbas together with these kings. 'Rejoicing, they approached the assembly of bhikkhus in the forest' means: with joyful and delighted minds, they came to this forest, to the assembly of the Bhikkhu Saṅgha.

338. Athāguṃ nāgasā nāgā, vesālā sahatacchakāti nāgasadahavāsikā ca vesālīvāsikā ca nāgā saha tacchakanāgaparisāya āgatāti attho. Kambalassatarāti kambalo ca assataro ca. Ete kira sinerupāde vasanti, supaṇṇehipi anuddharaṇīyā mahesakkhanāgā pāyāgā saha ñātibhīti payāgatitthavāsino ca saha ñātisaṅghena āgatā.

338. 'Then came the Nāgas of Nāgasa, of Vesālī, together with Tacchaka' means: the Nāgas dwelling in the Nāgasa Lake and the Nāgas dwelling in Vesālī came together with the assembly of the Tacchaka Nāga. 'Kambala and Assatara' means Kambala and Assatara. It is said they dwell at the foot of Sineru; they are mighty Nāgas who cannot be carried off even by the Supaṇṇas. 'The Pāyāgas with their kin' means: the Nāgas dwelling at the Payāga ford came together with their host of kinsmen.

Yāmunā dhataraṭṭhā cāti yamunavāsino ca dhataraṭṭhakule uppannā nāgā ca. Erāvaṇo mahānāgoti erāvaṇo ca devaputto, jātiyā nāgo na hoti. Nāgavohārena panesa vohariyati. Sopāgāti sopi āgato.

'The Yāmunā and the Dhataraṭṭhā' means: the Nāgas dwelling by the Yamunā and the Nāgas born in the Dhataraṭṭha clan. 'Erāvaṇa, the great Nāga' means: Erāvaṇa is a devaputta; he is not a Nāga by birth, but is referred to as a Nāga by convention. 'He too came' means: he also came.

Ye [M 2.0282] nāgarāje sahasā harantīti ye ime vuttappakāre nāge lobhābhibhūtā sāhasaṃ katvā haranti gaṇhanti. Dibbā dijā pakkhī visuddhacakkhūti dibbānubhāvato dibbā mātukucchito ca aṇḍakosato cāti dve vāre jātāti dijā pakkhayuttatāya pakkhī yojanasatantarepi yojanasahassantarepi nāge dassanasamatthacakkhutāya visuddhacakkhū. Vehāyasā [P 2.0689] te vanamajjhappattāti te ākāseneva imaṃ mahāvanaṃ sampattā. Citrā supaṇṇā iti tesa nāmanti tesaṃ “citrasupaṇṇā”ti nāmaṃ.

'Those who forcibly seize the Nāga kings' means: those who, overcome by greed, violently seize and take the aforementioned Nāgas. 'Divine, twice-born, winged, with pure vision' means: they are 'divine' due to their divine power; 'twice-born' (dijā) because they are born twice, from the mother's womb and from an eggshell; 'winged' (pakkhī) because they possess wings; and 'with pure vision' because their eyes are capable of seeing Nāgas even at a distance of a hundred or a thousand yojanas. 'Through the sky they reached the midst of the forest' means: they arrived at this great forest through the sky. 'Citrā Supaṇṇā is their name' means: their name is 'Citrasupaṇṇā'.

Abhayaṃ [V 2.0253] tadā nāgarājānamāsi, supaṇṇato khemamakāsi buddhoti tasmā sabbepi te aññamaññaṃ saṇhāhi vācāhi upavhayantā mittā viya bandhavā viya ca samullapantā sammodamānā āliṅgantā hatthe gaṇhantā aṃsakūṭe hatthaṃ ṭhapentā haṭṭhatuṭṭhacittā. Nāgā supaṇṇā saraṇamakaṃsu buddhanti buddhaṃyeva saraṇaṃ gatā.

'Then for the Nāga kings there was safety; from the Supaṇṇas the Buddha made security.' Therefore, all of them, addressing one another with gentle words, conversing and rejoicing together like friends and relatives, embracing, taking each other by the hand, placing a hand on the shoulder, with joyful and delighted minds. 'The Nāgas and Supaṇṇas took refuge in the Buddha' means: they went to the Buddha alone for refuge.

339. Jitā vajirahatthenāti indena devaraññā jitā. Samuddaṃ asurāsitāti mahāsamuddavāsino sujātāya asurakaññāya kāraṇā sabbepi bhātaro vāsavassete, iddhimanto yasassino.

339. 'Conquered by the one with vajra in hand' means: conquered by Indra, the king of the devas. 'The Asuras dwelt in the ocean' means: dwelling in the great ocean, on account of the asura-maiden Sujātā, all these are brothers of Vāsava, powerful and glorious.

Tesu kālakañcā mahābhismāti kālakañcā ca mahante bhiṃsane attabhāve māpetvā āgamiṃsu. Asurā dānaveghasāti dānaveghasā nāma aññe dhanuggahaasurā. Vepacitti sucitti ca, pahārādo namucī sahāti vepacittiasuro, sucittiasuro cāti ete ca asurā namuci ca māro devaputto etehi saheva āgato. Ime asurā mahāsamuddavāsino, ayaṃ paranimmitadevalokavāsī, kasmā etehi sahāgatoti? Acchandikattā. Tepi hi acchandikā abhabbā, ayampi tādisoyeva. Tasmā dhātuso saṃsandamāno āgato.

'Among them, the Kālakañcā, greatly terrifying' means: the Kālakañcā Asuras, having manifested great and terrifying forms, came. 'The Dānaveghasa Asuras' means: other asuras named Dānaveghasa, skilled with the bow. 'Vepacitti and Sucitti, Pahārāda, together with Namuci' means: the asura Vepacitti and the asura Sucitti, and these asuras, and Namuci, who is Māra the devaputta, came together with them. These asuras dwell in the great ocean, while this one dwells in the Paranimmitavasavattī deva-world. Why did he come with them? Because of a lack of wholesome desire. For they too lack wholesome desire and are incapable of progress, and he is just the same. Therefore, he came, associating with them according to his disposition.

Satañca baliputtānanti balino mahāasurassa puttānaṃ sataṃ. Sabbe verocanāmakāti sabbe attano mātulassa rāhusseva nāmadharā. Sannayhitvā balisenanti attano balisenaṃ sannayhitvā sabbe katasannāhāva hutvā. Rāhubhaddamupāgamunti rāhuasurindaṃ upasaṅkamiṃsu. Samayo [M 2.0283] dāni bhaddanteti bhaddaṃ tava hotu, samayo te bhikkhūnaṃ samitiṃ vanaṃ upasaṅkamitvā bhikkhusaṅghaṃ dassanāyāti attho.

'And a hundred sons of Bali' means: a hundred sons of the great asura Bali. 'All named Verocana' means: all bear the name of their maternal uncle, Rāhu. 'Having mustered Bali's army' means: having mustered their army of Bali, all stood fully armed. 'They approached the fortunate Rāhu' means: they approached Rāhu, the lord of asuras. 'Now is the time, good sir' means: 'May it be well with you. Now is the time for you to approach the assembly of bhikkhus in the forest to see the Bhikkhu Saṅgha.'

340. Āpo ca devā pathavī, tejo vāyo tadāgamunti āpokasiṇādīsu parikammaṃ katvā nibbattā āpotiādināmakā devā āgamuṃ. Varuṇā vāraṇā devā, somo ca yasasā sahāti varuṇadevatā[P 2.0690], vāraṇadevatā, somadevatāti evaṃ nāmakā ca devā yasasā nāma devena sahāgatāti attho. Mettākaruṇākāyikāti mettājhāne ca karuṇājhāne ca parikammaṃ katvā nibbattadevā. Āguṃ devā yasassinoti etepi mahāyasā devā āgatā.

340. 'The water devas, and earth, fire, and wind then came' means: the devas named 'Water' and so on, who were reborn after performing preliminary meditation on the water kasiṇa and so forth, came. 'The Varuṇa and Vāraṇa devas, and Soma with Yasas' means: the devas named Varuṇa, the devas named Vāraṇa, and the devas named Soma came together with the deva named Yasas. 'Those of the host of loving-kindness and compassion' means: devas reborn after performing preliminary meditation on the mettā-jhāna and the karuṇā-jhāna. 'The glorious devas came' means: these devas of great glory also came.

Dasete dasadhā kāyā, sabbe nānattavaṇṇinoti te dasadhā ṭhitā dasa devakāyā sabbe nīlādivasena nānattavaṇṇā āgatāti attho.

'These ten ten-fold hosts, all of various colors' means: those ten deva-hosts, established in ten groups, all came, being of various colors such as blue and so on.

Veṇḍū [V 2.0254] ca devāti veṇḍudevatā ca. Sahali cāti sahalidevatā ca. Asamā ca duve yamāti asamadevatā ca dve ca yamakā devā. Candassupanisā devā, candamāguṃ purakkhatvāti candanissitakā devā candaṃ purato katvā āgatā. Tathā sūriyanissitakā devā sūriyaṃ purakkhatvā. Nakkhattāni purakkhatvāti nakkhattanissitāpi devā nakkhattāni purato katvā āgatā. Āguṃ mandavalāhakāti vātavalāhakā, abbhavalāhakā, uṇhavalāhakā ete sabbepi valāhakāyikā “mandavalāhakā” nāma vuccanti. Tepi āgatāti attho. Vasūnaṃ vāsavo seṭṭho, sakkopāgā purindadoti vasūnaṃ devatānaṃ seṭṭho vāsavo yo sakkoti ca, purindadoti ca vuccati, sopi āgato.

'And the Veṇḍū devas' means: and the Veṇḍū devas. 'And Sahalī' means: and the Sahalī devas. 'And the Asamā and the two Yama' means: and the Asamā devas and the two Yama devas. 'The devas attendant on the moon came, placing the moon before them' means: the devas dependent on the moon came, having placed the moon in front. Likewise, the devas dependent on the sun, placing the sun before them. 'Placing the constellations before them' means: the devas dependent on the constellations also came, having placed the constellations in front. 'The Mandavalāhaka came' means: the wind-clouds, the mist-clouds, and the heat-clouds—all these of the cloud-host are called 'Mandavalāhaka'; they also came. 'Chief of the Vasus, Vāsava, Sakka came, Purindada' means: Vāsava, chief of the Vasu devas, who is called both Sakka and Purindada, he also came.

Dasete dasadhā kāyāti etepi dasa devakāyā dasadhāva āgatā. Sabbe nānattavaṇṇinoti nīlādivasena nānattavaṇṇā.

These ten groups of ten kinds—these ten divine hosts also came in ten groups. All of diverse colors—of various colors, such as blue and so on.

Athāguṃ sahabhū devāti atha sahabhū nāma devā āgatā. Jalamaggisikhārivāti aggisikhā viya jalantā. Jalamaggi ca sikhārivāti imāni tesaṃ nāmānītipi vuttaṃ. Ariṭṭhakā ca rojā cāti ariṭṭhakadevā ca rojadevā ca. Umāpupphanibhāsinoti umāpupphadevā nāma ete devā[M 2.0284]. Umāpupphasadisā hi tesaṃ sarīrābhā, tasmā “umāpupphanibhāsino”ti vuccanti.

Then came the Sahabhū deities—that is, deities named Sahabhū arrived. Blazing like a flame—that is, blazing like a flame. It is also said that 'Jalamaggi and Sikhārivā' were their names. The Ariṭṭhaka and Roja deities—that is, the Ariṭṭhaka deities and the Roja deities. Shining like Umā flowers—these deities are called Umāpuppha deities; for their bodies' radiance is like that of the Umā flower, therefore they are called 'shining like Umā flowers'.

Varuṇā sahadhammā cāti ete ca dve janā. Accutā ca anejakāti accutadevatā ca anejakadevatā ca. Suleyyarucirā [P 2.0691] āgunti suleyyā ca rucirā ca āgatā. Āguṃ vāsavanesinoti vāsavanesīdevā nāma āgatā. Dasete dasadhā kāyāti etepi dasadevakāyā dasadhāva āgatā.

Varuṇā and Sahadhammā—that is, these two beings. Accutā and Anejakā—that is, the Accuta deities and the Anejaka deities. Suleyyā and Rucirā have come—that is, Suleyyā and Rucirā have arrived. The Vāsavanesī have come—that is, deities named Vāsavanesī have arrived. These ten groups, each in tenfold form—that is, these ten groups of deities have arrived, each in tenfold form.

Samānā mahāsamānāti samānā ca mahāsamānā ca. Mānusā mānusuttamāti mānusā ca mānusuttamā ca. Khiḍḍāpadosikā āguṃ, āguṃ manopadosikāti khiḍḍāpadosikā manopadosikā ca devā āgatā.

Samānā and Mahāsamānā—that is, both the Samānā and the Mahāsamānā. Mānusā and Mānusuttamā—that is, both the Mānusā and the Mānusuttamā. The Khiḍḍāpadosikā have come, and the Manopadosikā have come—that is, the Khiḍḍāpadosikā and Manopadosikā deities have arrived.

Athāguṃ harayo devāti haridevā nāma āgatā. Ye ca lohitavāsinoti lohitavāsino ca āgatā. Pāragā mahāpāragāti ete ca duvidhā āgatā. Dasete dasadhā kāyāti etepi dasadevakāyā dasadhāva āgatā.

Then came the Harayo deities—that is, deities named Harideva have arrived. And those who dwell in Lohita—that is, the Lohitavāsino have also arrived. Pāragā and Mahāpāragā—that is, these two kinds have arrived. These ten groups, each in tenfold form—that is, these ten groups of deities have arrived, each in tenfold form.

Sukkā [V 2.0255] karambhā aruṇā, āguṃ veghanasā sahāti ete sukkādayo tayo, tehi saha veghanasā ca āgatā. Odātagayhā pāmokkhāti odātagayhā nāma pāmokkhadevā āgatā. Āguṃ devā vicakkhaṇāti vicakkhaṇā nāma devā āgatā.

Sukkā, Karambhā, and Aruṇā, and with them the Veghanasā have come—that is, these three beginning with Sukkā, and with them the Veghanasā have arrived. The Odātagayhā, the chiefs—that is, the chief deities named Odātagayhā have arrived. The Vicakkhaṇā deities have come—that is, deities named Vicakkhaṇā have arrived.

Sadāmattā hāragajāti sadāmattā ca hāragajā ca. Missakā ca yasassinoti yasasampannā missakadevā ca. Thanayaṃ āga pajjunnoti pajjunno ca devarājā thanayanto āgato. Yo disā abhivassatīti yo yaṃ yaṃ disaṃ yāti, tattha tattha devo vassati. Dasete dasadhā kāyāti etepi dasadevakāyā dasadhā āgatā.

Sadāmattā and Hāragajā—that is, both Sadāmattā and Hāragajā. The Missakā, rich in glory—that is, the glorious Missaka deities. Pajjunna, thundering, has come—that is, Pajjunna, the king of deities, has arrived thundering. Who rains down upon the directions—that is, whichever direction he goes, in that very place the god rains. These ten groups, each in tenfold form—that is, these ten groups of deities have arrived, each in tenfold form.

Khemiyā tusitā yāmāti khemiyā devā tusitapuravāsino ca yāmādevalokavāsino ca. Kathakā ca yasassinoti yasasampannā kathakadevā ca. Pāḷiyaṃ pana “kaṭṭhakā cā”ti likhanti. Lambītakā lāmaseṭṭhāti lambitakadevā ca lāmaseṭṭhadevā ca. Jotināmā ca āsavāti pabbatamatthake katanaḷaggikkhandho viya jotamānā jotidevā nāma atthi, te ca āsā ca devā āgatāti attho. Pāḷiyaṃ [M 2.0285] pana “jātināmā”ti likhanti. Āsā devatā chandavasena āsavāti vuttā. Nimmānaratino āguṃ, athāguṃ paranimmitā. Dasete dasadhā kāyāti etepi dasa devakāyā dasadhāva āgatā.

The Khemiyā, Tusitā, and Yāmā—that is, the Khemiyā deities, those dwelling in the Tusita city, and those dwelling in the Yāma divine realm. The Kathakā, rich in glory—that is, the glorious Kathaka deities. In the Pāḷi text, however, they write 'Kaṭṭhakā'. The Lambītakā and Lāmaseṭṭhā—that is, the Lambītaka deities and the Lāmaseṭṭha deities. The Jotināmā and the Āsavā—that is, there are deities named Joti, shining like a mass of reeds set ablaze on a mountaintop, and they, along with the Āsā deities, have arrived; this is the meaning. In the Pāḷi text, however, they write 'Jātināmā'. The Āsā deities are called Āsavā by way of poetic license. The Nimmānaratino have come, then the Paranimmitā have come. These ten groups, each in tenfold form—that is, these ten groups of deities have arrived, each in tenfold form.

Saṭṭhete [P 2.0692] devanikāyāti ete ca āpo ca devātiādikā cha dasakā saṭṭhi devanikāyā sabbe nīlādivasena nānattavaṇṇino. Nāmanvayena āgacchunti nāmabhāgena nāmakoṭṭhāsena āgatā. Ye caññe sadisā sahāti ye ca aññepi tehi sadisā vaṇṇatopi nāmatopi etādisāyeva sesacakkavāḷesu devā, tepi āgatāyevāti ekapadeneva kalāpaṃ viya puṭakaṃ viya ca katvā sabbā devatā niddisati.

These sixty groups of deities—that is, these sixty groups of deities, which are six sets of ten beginning with 'the Āpo deities', are all of diverse colors such as blue and so forth. They come according to their names—that is, they have arrived by their name-portions and name-divisions. And others who are similar, together with them—that is, other deities in the remaining world-systems who are just like them, similar in both color and name, they too have indeed arrived. Thus, having made them like a bundle or a package with a single phrase, he indicates all the deities.

Evaṃ dasasu lokadhātusahassesu devakāye niddisitvā idāni yadatthaṃ te āgatā, taṃ dassento pavuṭṭhajātinti gāthamāha. Tassattho – pavuṭṭhā vigatā jāti assāti ariyasaṅgho pavuṭṭhajāti nāma, taṃ pavuṭṭhajātiṃ rāgadosamohakhīlānaṃ abhāvā akhīlaṃ cattāro oghe taritvā ṭhitattā oghatiṇṇaṃ catunnaṃ āsavānaṃ abhāvena anāsavaṃ ariyasaṅghaṃ dakkhema passissāma. Tesaññeva oghānaṃ tiṇṇattā oghataraṃ āguṃ akaraṇato nāgaṃ. Asitātiganti kāḷakabhāvātītaṃ candaṃva siriyā virocamānaṃ dasabalañca dakkhema passissāmāti etadatthaṃ sabbepi te nāmanvayena āgacchuṃ, ye caññe sadisā sahāti.

Having thus indicated the groups of deities in the ten thousand world-systems, now, showing the purpose for which they had come, he spoke the verse beginning with 'pavuṭṭhajāti'. Its meaning is: The noble Saṅgha is called 'pavuṭṭhajāti' because birth has departed and ceased for it. We shall see and behold that noble Saṅgha, which has birth ceased; which is unimpeded due to the absence of the impediments of greed, hatred, and delusion; which has crossed the floods, due to having crossed the four floods and being established therein; and which is taintless due to the absence of the four taints. Because they have crossed those very floods, they are 'oghataraṃ' (crossers of the flood). Because they do no evil, they are 'nāga'. We shall see and behold the One who has gone beyond the dark state, shining with glory like the moon, the Ten-Powered One. It was for this purpose that all of them came according to their names, and others who were similar, together with them.

341. Idāni [V 2.0256] brahmāno dassento subrahmā paramatto cātiādimāha. Tattha subrahmāti eko brahmā. Paramattopi brahmāva. Puttā iddhimato sahāti ete iddhimato buddhassa bhagavato puttā ariyabrahmāno saheva āgatā. Sanaṅkumāro tisso cāti sanaṅkumāro ca tissamahābrahmā ca. Sopāgāti sopi āgato.

341. Now, indicating the brahmās, he spoke the verse beginning with 'Subrahmā and Paramatta'. Therein, Subrahmā is one brahmā. Paramatta is also a brahmā. 'Sons of the one with psychic power, together'—that is, these noble brahmās, sons of the Blessed One, the Buddha, who possesses psychic power, have arrived together. 'Sanaṅkumāra and Tissa'—that is, Sanaṅkumāra and Tissa the great brahmā. 'He also came'—that is, he too has arrived.

“Sahassaṃ brahmalokānaṃ, mahābrahmābhitiṭṭhati;

Upapanno jutimanto, bhismākāyo yasassi so”ti. –

“A thousand Brahma worlds, the Great Brahmā stands supreme; Arisen, radiant, of awesome body, glorious is he.”

Ettha [M 2.0286] sahassaṃ brahmalokānanti ekaṅguliyā ekasahassacakkavāḷe dasahi aṅgulīhi dasasahassicakkavāḷe ālokapharaṇasamatthānaṃ mahābrahmānaṃ sahassaṃ āgataṃ. Mahābrahmābhitiṭṭhatīti yattha ekeko mahābrahmā aññe brahme abhibhavitvā tiṭṭhati. Upapannoti [P 2.0693] brahmaloke nibbatto. Jutimantoti ānubhāvasampanno. Bhismākāyoti mahākāyo, dvīhi tīhi māgadhikehi gāmakkhettehi samappamāṇaattabhāvo. Yasassisoti attabhāvasirīsaṅkhātena yasena samannāgato.

Herein, 'a thousand Brahma worlds' means a thousand Great Brahmās have arrived, who are capable of spreading light throughout a thousand world-systems with one finger, and throughout ten thousand world-systems with ten fingers. 'The Great Brahmā stands supreme' means where each individual Great Brahmā stands, having surpassed the other brahmās. 'Arisen' means born in the Brahmā world. 'Radiant' means endowed with spiritual power. 'Of awesome body' means of great body, having a physical form of a size equal to two or three Magadhan village-fields. 'Glorious is he' means he is endowed with the glory known as the splendor of his physical form.

Dasettha issarā āguṃ, paccekavasavattinoti etasmiñca brahmasahasse ye pāṭiyekkaṃ pāṭiyekkaṃ vasaṃ vattenti, evarūpā dasa issarā mahābrahmāno āgatā. Tesañca majjhato āga, hārito parivāritoti tesaṃ brahmānaṃ majjhe hārito nāma mahābrahmā satasahassabrahmaparivāro āgato.

Ten lords came, each ruling independently—that is, among this thousandfold Brahmā realm, ten such sovereign Great Brahmās arrived who wield power individually. And from their midst came Hārita, surrounded by his retinue—that is, from among those Brahmās, the Great Brahmā named Hārita arrived, encircled by a hundred thousand Brahmā attendants.

342. Te ca sabbe abhikkante, sainde deve sabrahmaketi te sabbepi sakkaṃ devarājānaṃ jeṭṭhakaṃ katvā āgate devakāye, hāritamahābrahmānaṃ jeṭṭhakaṃ katvā āgate brahmakāye ca. Mārasenā abhikkāmīti mārasenā abhigatā. Passa kaṇhassa mandiyanti kāḷakassa mārasa bālabhāvaṃ passatha.

342. And all those who came forward, the gods with Indra and the Brahmās—that is, all those groups of deities who arrived with Sakka, the king of deities, as their chief, and all those groups of Brahmās who arrived with the Great Brahmā Hārita as their chief. 'The army of Māra is advancing'—that is, the army of Māra has arrived. 'See the folly of the Dark One'—that is, behold the childishness of Māra the Dark One.

Etha gaṇhatha bandhathāti evaṃ attano parisaṃ āṇāpesi. Rāgena baddhamatthu voti sabbaṃ vo idaṃ devamaṇḍalaṃ rāgena baddhaṃ hotu. Samantā parivāretha, mā vo muñcittha koci nanti tumhākaṃ ekopi etesu ekampi mā muñci. “Mā vo muñcethā”tipi pāṭho, esevattho.

‘Come, seize, and bind!’—thus he commanded his assembly. ‘Let them be bound by lust’—that is, may this entire divine assembly be bound by lust. ‘Surround them on all sides, let none of you release any of them’—that is, let not even one of you release even one among them. The reading ‘Mā vo muñcethā’ also exists; the meaning is the same.

Iti tattha mahāseno, kaṇho senaṃ apesayīti evaṃ tattha mahāsamaye mahāseno māro mārasenaṃ [V 2.0257] apesayi. Pāṇinā talamāhaccāti hatthena pathavītalaṃ paharitvā. Saraṃ katvāna bheravanti māravibhiṃsakadassanatthaṃ bhayānakaṃ sarañca katvā.

‘Thus the great-armied Dark One sent forth his army there’—that is, thus at that great assembly, the great-armied Māra sent forth the army of Māra. ‘Striking the ground with his palm’—that is, striking the surface of the earth with his hand. ‘And making a terrifying sound’—that is, and making a fearful sound to display Māra's frightening power.

Yathā pāvussako megho, thanayanto savijjukoti savijjuko pāvussakamegho viya mahāgajjitaṃ gajjanto. Tadā so paccudāvattīti tasmiṃ samaye so māro taṃ vibhiṃsanakaṃ dassetvā paṭinivatto[M 2.0287]. Saṅkuddho asayaṃ vaseti suṭṭhu kuddho kupito kañci vase vattetuṃ [P 2.0694] asakkonto asayaṃvase asayaṃvasī attano vasena akāmako hutvā nivatto. Bhagavā kira “ayaṃ māro imaṃ mahāsamāgamaṃ disvā ‘abhisamayantarāyaṃ karissāmī’ti antarantare mārasenaṃ pesetvā māraṃ vibhiṃsakaṃ dassetī”ti aññāsi. Pakati cesā bhagavato, yattha abhisamayo na bhavissati, tattha māraṃ vibhiṃsakaṃ dassentaṃ na nivāreti. Yattha pana abhisamayo hoti, tattha yathā parisā neva mārassa rūpaṃ passati, na saddaṃ suṇāti, evaṃ adhiṭṭhātīti. Imasmiñca samāgame mahābhisamayo bhavissati, tasmā yathā devatā neva tassa rūpaṃ passanti, na saddaṃ suṇanti, evaṃ adhiṭṭhāsi. Tena vuttaṃ –“tadā so paccudāvatti, saṅkuddho asayaṃvase”ti.

‘Like a rain cloud in season, thundering with lightning’—that is, thundering with a great roar like a rain cloud of the rainy season with lightning. ‘Then he turned back’—that is, at that time Māra, having shown that terrifying display, retreated. ‘Enraged and not his own master’—that is, thoroughly enraged and angry, unable to bring anyone under his control, not his own master, he retreated unwillingly. The Blessed One, it is said, understood: “This Māra, seeing this great assembly, thinks, ‘I will create an obstacle to their realization,’ and so, sending his army in between, he displays his frightful form.” Now, it is the nature of the Blessed One that where realization will not occur, he does not prevent Māra from showing his terrifying form. But where realization is to take place, he resolves in such a way that the assembly neither sees Māra’s form nor hears his sound. And in this assembly a great realization was to occur; therefore, he resolved in such a way that the deities would neither see his form nor hear his sound. Hence it was said: ‘Then he turned back, enraged and not his own master.’

343. Tañca sabbaṃ abhiññāya, vavatthitvāna cakkhumāti taṃ sabbaṃ bhagavā jānitvā vavatthapetvā ca.

343. ‘And having fully understood all that, the One with Vision determined’—that is, the Blessed One, having known and determined all that.

Mārasenā abhikkantā, te vijānātha bhikkhavoti bhikkhave mārasenā abhikkantā, te tumhe attano anurūpaṃ vijānātha, phalasamāpattiṃ samāpajjathāti vadati. Ātappamakarunti phalasamāpattiṃ pavisanatthāya vīriyaṃ ārabhiṃsu. Vītarāgehi pakkāmunti māro ca mārasenā ca vītarāgehi ariyehi dūratova apakkamuṃ. Nesaṃ lomāpi iñjayunti tesaṃ vītarāgānaṃ lomānipi na cālayiṃsu. Atha māro bhikkhusaṅghaṃ ārabbha imaṃ gāthaṃ abhāsi –

‘The army of Māra has advanced; understand this, O bhikkhus!’ This means, ‘O bhikkhus, the army of Māra has advanced; understand this as is fitting for you, and enter the attainment of fruition.’ ‘They exerted themselves with ardor’ means they aroused energy to enter the attainment of fruition. ‘They departed from those free from lust’ means Māra and Māra’s army departed from afar from the noble ones who were free from lust. ‘Not even a hair of theirs did they stir’ means they could not stir even a hair of those free from lust. Then Māra, concerning the community of bhikkhus, spoke this verse:

“Sabbe vijitasaṅgāmā, bhayātītā yasassino;

Modanti saha bhūtehi, sāvakā te janesutā”ti.

“All have won the battle, gone beyond fear, and are renowned; they rejoice together with the noble ones, your disciples, well-known among the people.”

Tattha modanti saha bhūtehīti dasabalassa sāsane bhūtehi sañjātehi ariyehi saddhiṃ modanti pamodanti. Janesutāti jane vissutā pākaṭā abhiññātā.

Therein, ‘they rejoice together with the noble ones’ means that in the Dispensation of the Ten-Powered One, they rejoice and delight together with the noble ones who have come into being. ‘Well-known among the people’ means they are well-known, manifest, and recognized among the people.

Idaṃ [V 2.0258] pana mahāsamayasuttaṃ nāma devatānaṃ piyaṃ manāpaṃ, tasmā maṅgalaṃ vadantena abhinavaṭṭhānesu idameva suttaṃ vattabbaṃ. Devatā kira –“imaṃ suttaṃ suṇissāmā”ti [P 2.0695] ohitasotā vicaranti. Desanāpariyosāne panassa [M 2.0288] koṭisatasahassadevatā arahattaṃ pattā, sotāpannādīnaṃ gaṇanā natthi.

Now, this Mahāsamaya Sutta is beloved and pleasing to the deities. Therefore, when reciting a blessing on a new occasion, this very sutta should be recited. For it is said that the deities wander about with attentive ears, thinking, ‘We shall listen to this sutta.’ At the conclusion of the discourse, a hundred thousand koṭis of deities attained arahantship, and the number of those who became stream-enterers and so forth was beyond counting.

Devatānañcassa piyamanāpabhāve idaṃ vatthu – koṭipabbatavihāre kira nāgaleṇadvāre nāgarukkhe ekā devadhītā vasati. Eko daharo antoleṇe imaṃ suttaṃ sajjhāyati. Devadhītā sutvā suttapariyosāne mahāsaddena sādhukāramadāsi. Ko esoti. Ahaṃ, bhante, devadhītāti. Kasmā sādhukāramadāsīti? Bhante, dasabalena mahāvane nisīditvā kathitadivase imaṃ suttaṃ sutvā ajja assosiṃ, bhagavatā kathitato ekakkharampi ahāpetvā suggahito ayaṃ dhammo tumhehīti. Dasabalassa kathayato sutaṃ tayāti? Āma, bhanteti. Mahā kira devatāsannipāto ahosi, tvaṃ kattha ṭhitā suṇīti?

Regarding its being beloved and pleasing to the deities, there is this story: It is said that at Koṭipabbata Monastery, near the entrance of the Nāga Cave, a deva-daughter dwells in a Nāga tree. A young monk inside the cave was reciting this sutta. Hearing it, the deva-daughter, at the end of the sutta, loudly expressed her approval. ‘Who is that?’ ‘I am a deva-daughter, venerable sir.’ ‘Why did you express approval?’ ‘Venerable sir, having heard this sutta on the day it was taught by the Ten-Powered One as he was seated in the Great Forest, today I heard it again. This Dhamma has been well grasped by you, without omitting even a single syllable from what the Blessed One taught.’ ‘Did you hear it when the Ten-Powered One was teaching?’ ‘Yes, venerable sir.’ ‘It is said there was a great assembly of deities. Where were you standing when you listened?’

Ahaṃ, bhante, mahāvanavāsiyā devatā, mahesakkhāsu pana devatāsu āgacchantīsu jambudīpe okāsaṃ nālatthaṃ, atha imaṃ tambapaṇṇidīpaṃ āgantvā jambukolapaṭṭane ṭhatvā sotuṃ āraddhamhi, tatrāpi mahesakkhāsu devatāsu āgacchantīsu anukkamena paṭikkamamānā rohaṇajanapade mahāgāmassa piṭṭhibhāgato samudde galappamāṇaṃ udakaṃ pavisitvā tattha ṭhitā assosinti. Tuyhaṃ ṭhitaṭṭhānato dūre satthāraṃ passasi devateti? Kiṃ kathetha, bhante, satthā mahāvane dhammaṃ desento nirantaraṃ mamaññeva oloketīti maññamānā otappamānā ūmīsu nilayāmīti.

‘Venerable sir, I am a deity dwelling in the Great Forest. But when the deities of great power came, I could not find a place in Jambudīpa. So I came to this island of Tambapaṇṇi and began to listen, standing at the port of Jambukola. Even there, as deities of great power arrived, I gradually retreated until, in the country of Rohaṇa, behind a large village, I entered the ocean up to my neck and stood there listening.’ ‘Deity, from where you were standing, so far away, could you see the Teacher?’ ‘What are you saying, venerable sir? While the Teacher was teaching the Dhamma in the Great Forest, it seemed to me that he was constantly looking only at me, and so, feeling a sense of moral shame, I kept hiding among the waves.’

Taṃ divasaṃ kira koṭisatasahassadevatā arahattaṃ pattā, tumhepi tadā arahattaṃ pattāti? Natthi, bhante. Anāgāmiphalaṃ pattattha maññeti? Natthi, bhante. Sakadāgāmiphalaṃ pattattha maññeti? Natthi, bhante. Tayo magge pattā devatā kira gaṇanapathaṃ [P 2.0696] atītā, sotāpannā jātattha maññeti? Devatā taṃ divasaṃ sotāpattiphalaṃ pattattā harāyamānā –“apucchitabbaṃ pucchati ayyo”ti āha. Tato naṃ so bhikkhu āha – “sakkā pana devate, tava attabhāvaṃ amhākaṃ dassetu”nti? Na sakkā bhante sakalakāyaṃ [M 2.0289] dassetuṃ, aṅgulipabbamattaṃ dassessāmi ayyassāti kuñcikachiddena aṅguliṃ antoleṇābhimukhaṃ akāsi, candasahassasūriyasahassauggamanakālo viya ahosi. Devadhītā “appamattā, bhante, hothā”ti daharabhikkhuṃ [V 2.0259] vanditvā agamāsi. Evaṃ imaṃ suttaṃ devatānaṃ piyaṃ manāpaṃ, mamāyanti naṃ devatāti.

‘On that day, it is said, a hundred thousand koṭis of deities attained arahantship. Did you too attain arahantship then?’ ‘No, venerable sir.’ ‘I suppose you attained the fruit of non-returning?’ ‘No, venerable sir.’ ‘I suppose you attained the fruit of once-returning?’ ‘No, venerable sir.’ ‘It is said that the deities who attained the three paths were beyond counting. I suppose you became stream-enterers?’ The deity, being ashamed of having attained the fruit of stream-entry that day, said, ‘The venerable one asks what should not be asked!’ Then that bhikkhu said to her, ‘Deity, is it possible for you to show us your form?’ ‘It is not possible, venerable sir, to show my entire body. I will show the venerable one the measure of a finger-joint.’ Making a finger appear through a keyhole facing into the cave, it was like the rising of a thousand moons and a thousand suns. The deva maiden, saying, ‘Be heedful, venerable sir,’ paid homage to the young bhikkhu and departed. Thus, this discourse is dear and delightful to the deities; they cherish it.

Iti sumaṅgalavilāsiniyā dīghanikāyaṭṭhakathāyaṃ

Thus in the Sumaṅgalavilāsinī, the Commentary on the Dīgha Nikāya,

Mahāsamayasuttavaṇṇanā niṭṭhitā.

The Commentary on the Mahāsamaya Sutta is concluded.

8. Sakkapañhasuttavaṇṇanā

8. The Commentary on the Sakkapañha Sutta

Nidānavaṇṇanā

The Commentary on the Introduction

344. Evaṃ [P 3.0697][V 2.0260][M 2.0290] me sutanti sakkapañhasuttaṃ. Tatrāyamanuttānapadavaṇṇanā – ambasaṇḍā nāma brāhmaṇagāmoti so kira gāmo ambasaṇḍānaṃ avidūre niviṭṭho, tasmā “ambasaṇḍā” tveva vuccati. Vediyake pabbateti so kira pabbato pabbatapāde jātena maṇivedikāsadisena nīlavanasaṇḍena samantā parikkhitto, tasmā ‘vediyakapabbato’ tveva saṅkhyaṃ gato. Indasālaguhāyanti pubbepi sā dvinnaṃ pabbatānaṃ antare guhā, indasālarukkho cassā dvāre, tasmā ‘indasālaguhā’ti saṅkhyaṃ gatā. Atha naṃ kuṭṭehi parikkhipitvā dvāravātapānāni yojetvā supariniṭṭhitasudhākammamālākammalatākammavicittaṃ leṇaṃ katvā bhagavato adaṃsu. Purimavohāravasena pana “indasālaguhā” tveva naṃ sañjānanti. Taṃ sandhāya vuttaṃ ‘indasālaguhāya’nti.

344. "Thus have I heard"—this is the Sakkapañha Sutta. Herein is the explanation of the obscure terms. "Ambasaṇḍā" is the name of a brahmin village; it is said that village was situated not far from mango groves, hence it is called "Ambasaṇḍā." "On the Vediyaka mountain": it is said that mountain was surrounded on all sides by a blue forest grove resembling a jeweled terrace, which had grown at the foot of the mountain; hence it came to be known as "Vediyaka mountain." "In the Indasāla cave": even previously, that was a cave between two mountains, and an Indasāla tree was at its entrance; hence it came to be known as "Indasāla cave." Then, enclosing it with walls and fitting it with doors and windows, they made it a dwelling adorned with perfectly finished plasterwork, garland-work, and creeper-work, and gave it to the Blessed One. But by its former designation, they still knew it as "Indasāla cave." It is with reference to this that it is said, "in the Indasāla cave."

Ussukkaṃ udapādīti dhammiko ussāho uppajji. Nanu ca esa abhiṇhadassāvī bhagavato, na so devatāsannipāto nāma atthi, yatthāyaṃ na āgatapubbo, sakkena sadiso appamādavihārī devaputto nāma natthi. Atha kasmā buddhadassanaṃ anāgatapubbassa viya assa ussāho udapādīti? Maraṇabhayena santajjitattā. Tasmiṃ kirassa samaye āyu parikkhīṇo, so pañca pubbanimittāni disvā “parikkhīṇo [P 3.0698] dāni me āyū”ti aññāsi. Yesañca devaputtānaṃ maraṇanimittāni āvi bhavanti, tesu ye parittakena puññakammena devaloke nibbattā, te “kuhiṃ nu kho idāni nibbattissāmā”ti bhayaṃ santāsaṃ āpajjanti. Ye katabhīruttānā bahuṃ puññaṃ katvā nibbattā, te attanā dinnadānaṃ rakkhitasīlaṃ bhāvitabhāvanañca āgamma “uparidevaloke sampattiṃ anubhavissāmā”ti na bhāyanti.

An eagerness arose—that is, a righteous enthusiasm arose. Was he not, indeed, one who frequently saw the Blessed One? There was no assembly of deities where he had not gone before; there is no deva-son equal to Sakka who dwells so heedfully. Then why did enthusiasm arise in him to see the Buddha as if he had never come before? Because he was terrified by the fear of death. At that time, it is said, his lifespan was nearly exhausted, and seeing the five portents, he understood, 'Now my lifespan is nearly exhausted.' And among those deva-sons for whom the signs of death become apparent, those who were reborn in the deva-world through meager meritorious deeds become fearful and terrified, thinking, 'Where now shall we be reborn?' But those who were reborn having done much merit, having made a protection against fear, relying on the gifts they had given, the virtue they had guarded, and the meditation they had cultivated, do not fear, thinking, 'We shall experience prosperity in a higher deva-world.'

Sakko [V 2.0261] pana devarājā pubbanimittāni disvā dasayojanasahassaṃ devanagaraṃ, yojanasahassubbedhaṃ vejayantaṃ, tiyojanasatikaṃ sudhammadevasabhaṃ, yojanasatubbedhaṃ pāricchattakaṃ, saṭṭhiyojanikaṃ paṇḍukambalasilaṃ, aḍḍhatiyā nāṭakakoṭiyo dvīsu devalokesu devaparisaṃ, nandanavanaṃ, cittalatāvanaṃ[M 2.0291], missakavanaṃ, phārusakavananti etaṃ sabbasampattiṃ oloketvā “nassati vata bho me ayaṃ sampattī”ti bhayābhibhūto ahosi.

But Sakka, the king of the devas, seeing the portents, surveyed all this prosperity: the ten-thousand-yojana celestial city, the thousand-yojana-high Vejayanta palace, the three-hundred-yojana Sudhamma assembly hall, the hundred-yojana-high Pāricchattaka tree, the sixty-yojana Paṇḍukambala stone, two and a half crores of dancing girls, the assembly of devas in the two deva-worlds, the Nandana Grove, the Cittalatā Grove, the Missaka Grove, and the Phārusaka Grove. Observing all this, he became overwhelmed with fear, thinking, 'Alas, this prosperity of mine is perishing!'

Tato “atthi nu kho koci samaṇo vā brāhmaṇo vā lokapitāmaho mahābrahmā vā, yo me hadayanissitaṃ sokasallaṃ samuddharitvā imaṃ sampattiṃ thāvaraṃ kareyyā”ti olokento kañci adisvā puna addasa “mādisānaṃ satasahassānampi uppannaṃ sokasallaṃ sammāsambuddho uddharituṃ paṭibalo”ti. Athevaṃ parivitakkentassa tena kho pana samayena sakkassa devānamindassa ussukkaṃ udapādi bhagavantaṃ dassanāya.

Then, searching, 'Is there any ascetic or brahmin, or the Great Brahmā, the Grandfather of the World, who could pull out this arrow of sorrow lodged in my heart and make this prosperity permanent?' and seeing no one, he then saw, 'The Perfectly Enlightened One is capable of extracting the arrow of sorrow that has arisen even in hundreds of thousands of beings like myself.' As he was reflecting in this way, at that very moment an eagerness to see the Blessed One arose in Sakka, the lord of the devas.

Kahaṃ nu kho bhagavā etarahi viharatīti katarasmiṃ janapade kataraṃ nagaraṃ upanissāya kassa paccaye paribhuñjanto kassa amataṃ dhammaṃ desayamāno viharatīti. Addasā khoti addakkhi paṭivijjhi. Mārisāti piyavacanametaṃ, devatānaṃ pāṭiyekko vohāro. Niddukkhātipi vuttaṃ hoti. Kasmā panesa deve āmantesi? Sahāyatthāya. Pubbe kiresa bhagavati saḷalaghare viharante ekakova dassanāya agamāsi. Satthā “aparipakkaṃ tāvassa ñāṇaṃ, katipāhaṃ pana atikkamitvā mayi indasālaguhāyaṃ viharante pañca pubbanimittāni disvā maraṇabhayabhīto dvīsu devalokesu devatāhi saddhiṃ upasaṅkamitvā cuddasa pañhe pucchitvā upekkhāpañhavissajjanāvasāne asītiyā devatāsahassehi saddhiṃ sotāpattiphale patiṭṭhahissatī”ti cintetvā okāsaṃ nākāsi. So “mama pubbepi [P 3.0699] ekakassa gatattā satthārā okāso na kato, addhā me natthi maggaphalassa upanissayo, ekassa pana upanissaye sati cakkavāḷapariyantāyapi parisāya bhagavā dhammaṃ desetiyeva. Avassaṃ kho pana dvīsu devalokesu kassaci devassa upanissayo bhavissati, taṃ sandhāya satthā dhammaṃ desessati. Taṃ sutvā ahampi attano domanassaṃ vūpasamessāmī”ti cintetvā sahāyatthāya āmantesi.

“Where indeed does the Blessed One now dwell? In which country, near which city, enjoying whose requisites, and to whom teaching the deathless Dhamma does he dwell?” The phrase 'Addasā kho' means 'he saw, he penetrated.' 'Mārisa' is a term of endearment, a special expression for devas; it is also said to mean 'free from suffering.' But why did he address the devas? For the sake of companionship. Previously, it is said, when the Blessed One was dwelling in the Salala House, he went alone to see him. The Teacher, thinking, 'His knowledge is not yet mature; but after a few days have passed, when I am dwelling in the Indasāla Cave, having seen the five premonitory signs and being terrified by the fear of death, he will approach with the devas from the two deva-worlds, and after asking fourteen questions, at the conclusion of the answer to the question on equanimity, he will become established in the fruit of stream-entry along with eighty thousand devas,' did not grant him an opportunity. He thought, 'Since previously, when I went alone, the Teacher did not grant me an opportunity, surely I have no supporting condition for the path and fruit. However, if there is a supporting condition for even one person, the Blessed One teaches the Dhamma even to an assembly extending to the limits of the world-system. Surely, in the two deva-worlds, there must be some deva who has the supporting condition; with that one in mind, the Teacher will teach the Dhamma. Having heard it, I too will pacify my own sorrow.' Thinking thus, he addressed them for the sake of companionship.

Evaṃ bhaddaṃ tavāti kho devā tāvatiṃsāti evaṃ hotu mahārāja, gacchāma bhagavantaṃ dassanāya, dullabho buddhuppādo, bhaddaṃ tava, yo tvaṃ “pabbatakīḷaṃ nadīkīḷaṃ gacchāmā”ti avatvā [V 2.0262] amhe evarūpesu ṭhānesu niyojesīti. Paccassosunti tassa vacanaṃ sirasā sampaṭicchiṃsu.

The Tāvatiṃsa devas said, 'So be it, great king; may it be well with you. We shall go to see the Blessed One, for the arising of a Buddha is rare. It is well with you that, without saying, “Let us go to play on the mountain or in the river,” you directed us to such a matter.' The phrase 'Paccassosuṃ' means they accepted his words with their heads.

345. Pañcasikhaṃ [M 2.0292] gandhabbadevaputtaṃ āmantesīti deve tāva āmantetu, imaṃ kasmā visuṃ āmantesi? Okāsakaraṇatthaṃ. Evaṃ kirassa ahosi “dvīsu devalokesu devatā gahetvā dhurena paharantassa viya satthāraṃ upasaṅkamituṃ na yuttaṃ, ayaṃ pana pañcasikho dasabalassa upaṭṭhāko vallabho icchiticchitakkhaṇe gantvā pañhaṃ pucchitvā dhammaṃ suṇāti, imaṃ purato pesetvā okāsaṃ kāretvā iminā katokāse upasaṅkamitvā pañhaṃ pucchissāmī”ti okāsakaraṇatthaṃ āmantesi.

345. The phrase 'He addressed Pañcasikha, the gandhabba deva-son' implies: He had already addressed the devas, so why did he address this one separately? For the purpose of creating an opportunity. It is said that it occurred to him thus: 'It is not fitting to approach the Teacher having taken devas from two deva-worlds, as if striking him with the yoke of a cart. This Pañcasikha, however, is an attendant of the Ten-Powered One and is favored by him; at any moment he wishes, he can go, ask a question, and listen to the Dhamma. I will send him ahead to create an opportunity, and when the opportunity has been created by him, I will approach and ask my questions.' Thus, he addressed him for the purpose of creating an opportunity.

Evaṃ bhaddaṃ tavāti so “evaṃ mahārāja, hotu, bhaddaṃ tava, yo tvaṃ maṃ ‘ehi, mārisa, uyyānakīḷādīni vā naṭasamajjādīni vā dassanāya gacchāmā’ti avatvā ‘buddhaṃ passissāma, dhammaṃ sossāmā’ti vadasī”ti daḷhataraṃ upatthambhento devānamindassa vacanaṃ paṭissutvā anucariyaṃ sahacaraṇaṃ ekato gamanaṃ upāgami.

The phrase 'So be it, may it be well with you' means that he, further encouraging him, said: 'So be it, great king. May it be well with you, since without saying to me, “Come, friend, let us go to see pleasure gardens or theatrical shows,” you say instead, “We shall see the Buddha, we shall hear the Dhamma.”' Having thus consented to the words of the lord of the devas, he undertook to be his attendant, to accompany him, and to go together with him.

Tattha beluvapaṇḍunti beluvapakkaṃ viya paṇḍuvaṇṇaṃ. Tassa kira sovaṇṇamayaṃ pokkharaṃ, indanīlamayo daṇḍo, rajatamayā tantiyo, pavāḷamayā veṭhakā, vīṇāpattakaṃ gāvutaṃ, tantibandhanaṭṭhānaṃ gāvutaṃ, upari daṇḍako gāvutanti tigāvutappamāṇā vīṇā. Iti so taṃ vīṇaṃ ādāya samapaññāsamucchanā mucchetvā agganakhehi paharitvā madhuraṃ gītassaraṃ nicchāretvā sesadeve sakkassa gamanakālaṃ [P 3.0700] jānāpento ekamantaṃ aṭṭhāsi. Evaṃ tassa gītavāditasaññāya sannipatite devagaṇe atha kho sakko devānamindo…pe… vediyake pabbate paccuṭṭhāsi.

Therein, 'Beluvapaṇḍu' means having a pale-yellow color like a ripe beluva fruit. It is said that its soundbox was made of gold, its neck of sapphire, its strings of silver, and its frets of coral. The body of the lute was a gāvuta, the place where the strings were fastened was a gāvuta, and the upper part of the neck was a gāvuta—thus the lute was three gāvutas in measure. Taking that lute and tuning its fifty modes, he struck the strings with his fingertips, produced a sweet musical sound, and, while making known to the other devas the time of Sakka's departure, he stood to one side. Thus, when the host of devas had assembled at the signal of his singing and playing, then Sakka, the lord of the devas... appeared on the Vediyaka mountain.

346. Atiriva obhāsajātoti aññesu divasesu ekasseva devassa vā mārassa vā brahmuno vā obhāsena obhāsajāto hoti, taṃdivasaṃ pana dvīsu devalokesu devatānaṃ obhāsena atiriva obhāsajāto ekapajjoto sahassacandasūriyauggatakālasadiso ahosi. Parito gāmesu manussāti samantā gāmesu manussā. Pakatisāyamāsakāleyeva kira gāmamajjhe dārakesu kīḷantesu tattha sakko agamāsi, tasmā manussā passitvā evamāhaṃsu. Nanu ca majjhimayāme devatā bhagavantaṃ upasaṅkamanti, ayaṃ kasmā [M 2.0293] paṭhamayāmassāpi purimabhāgeyeva āgatoti? Maraṇabhayeneva tajjitattā. Kiṃsu nāmāti kiṃsu nāma bho etaṃ, ko nu kho ajja mahesakkho devo vā brahmā vā bhagavantaṃ pañhaṃ pucchituṃ dhammaṃ sotuṃ upasaṅkamanto, kathaṃsu [V 2.0263] nāma bho bhagavā pañhaṃ vissajjessati dhammaṃ desessati, lābhā amhākaṃ, yesaṃ no evaṃ devatānaṃ kaṅkhāvinodako satthā avidūre vihāre vasati, ye labhāma thālakabhikkhampi kaṭacchubhikkhampi dātunti saṃviggā lomahaṭṭhajātā uddhaggalomā hutvā dasanakhasamodhānasamujjalaṃ añjaliṃ sirasmiṃ patiṭṭhapetvā namassamānā aṭṭhaṃsu.

346. The phrase 'an exceedingly great radiance arose' means: on other days, a radiance arises from the light of a single deva, or a Māra, or a Brahmā. But on that day, due to the radiance of the devas from the two deva-worlds, an exceedingly great radiance arose, a single blaze of light like the rising of a thousand moons and a thousand suns. 'The people in the surrounding villages' means the people in the villages all around. It is said that Sakka arrived just at the normal evening mealtime, while children were playing in the middle of the village. Therefore, the people saw it and spoke thus. 'But do not devas approach the Blessed One in the middle watch of the night? Why has this one come in the very first part of the first watch?' Because he was threatened by the fear of death. 'What can this be?' means: 'Sirs, what can this be? What mighty deva or brahmā is approaching the Blessed One today to ask a question and hear the Dhamma? Sirs, how will the Blessed One answer the question and teach the Dhamma? It is a great gain for us, for whom the Teacher, the dispeller of the doubts of devas, dwells in a monastery not far away, and we who have the opportunity to give even a small bowlful or a ladleful of almsfood!' Thus, filled with spiritual urgency, their hair standing on end, they placed their joined hands, shining with their ten assembled fingernails, upon their heads and stood paying homage.

347. Durupasaṅkamāti dupayirupāsiyā. Ahaṃ sarāgo sadoso samoho, satthā vītarāgo vītadoso vītamoho, tasmā dupayirupāsiyā tathāgatā mādisena. Jhāyīti lakkhaṇūpanijjhānena ca ārammaṇūpanijjhānena ca jhāyī. Tasmiññeva jhāne ratāti jhānaratā. Tadantaraṃ paṭisallīnāti tadantaraṃ paṭisallīnā sampati paṭisallīnā vā. Tasmā na kevalaṃ jhāyī jhānaratāti durupasaṅkamā, idānimeva paṭisallīnātipi durupasaṅkamā. Pasādeyyāsīti ārādheyyāsi, okāsaṃ me kāretvā dadeyyāsīti vadati. Beluvapaṇḍuvīṇaṃ ādāyāti nanu pubbeva ādinnāti? Āma[P 3.0701], ādinnā. Maggagamanavasena pana aṃsakūṭe laggitā, idāni naṃ vāmahatthe ṭhapetvā vādanasajjaṃ katvā ādiyi. Tena vuttaṃ “ādāyā”ti.

347. "Difficult to approach" means difficult to be approached. I am with passion, with aversion, with delusion; the Teacher is without passion, without aversion, without delusion. Therefore, the Tathāgatas are difficult to be approached by one like me. "A meditator" means one who meditates through contemplation of characteristics and through contemplation of an object. "Delighting in jhāna" means one who delights in that very jhāna. "Secluded in the meantime" means secluded in the meantime, or secluded at present. Therefore, not only because he is a meditator and delights in jhāna is he difficult to approach, but also because he is secluded right now is he difficult to approach. "You should please" means you should gratify; he says, "Having made an opportunity for me, you should give it." Regarding "taking the pale beluva-wood lute": Was it not already taken before? Yes, it was taken. But, on account of traveling on the road, it was hung on his shoulder. Now, placing it in his left hand and preparing it for playing, he took it. Therefore, it was said, "taking."

Pañcasikhagītagāthāvaṇṇanā

The Commentary on the Verses of Pañcasikha's Song

348. Assāvesīti sāvesi. Buddhūpasañhitāti buddhaṃ ārabbha buddhaṃ nissayaṃ katvā pavattāti attho. Sesapadesupi eseva nayo.

348. "He caused to hear" means he made known. "Connected with the Buddha" means arisen concerning the Buddha, having taken the Buddha as a support. This same method applies to the remaining terms as well.

Vande te pitaraṃ bhadde, timbaruṃ sūriyavacchaseti ettha sūriyavacchasāti sūriyasamānasarīrā. Tassā kira devadhītāya pādantato rasmi uṭṭhahitvā kesantaṃ ārohati, tasmā bālasūriyamaṇḍalasadisā khāyati, iti naṃ “sūriyavacchasā”ti sañjānanti. Taṃ sandhāyāha – “bhadde, sūriyavacchase, tava pitaraṃ timbaruṃ gandhabbadevarājānaṃ vandāmī”ti. Yena jātāsi kalyāṇīti yena [M 2.0294] kāraṇabhūtena yaṃ timbaruṃ devarājānaṃ nissāya tvaṃ jātā, kalyāṇī sabbaṅgasobhanā. Ānandajananī mamāti mayhaṃ pītisomanassavaḍḍhanī.

Here, in the verse "I pay homage to your father, good lady, Timbaru, O Sūriyavacchasā," "Sūriyavacchasā" means one whose body is like the sun. It is said that for that goddess, a ray of light, rising from the sole of her foot, ascends to the tip of her hair. Therefore, she appears like the disk of the rising sun, and thus they know her as "Sūriyavacchasā." With reference to her, he said: "Good lady, O Sūriyavacchasā, I pay homage to your father, Timbaru, the king of the gandhabbas." "By whom you were born, O beautiful one" means: by which cause, depending on which divine king Timbaru, you were born. "Beautiful one" means beautiful in all limbs. "Mother of my joy" means the increaser of my joy and gladness.

Vātova sedataṃ kantoti yathā sañjātasedānaṃ sedaharaṇatthaṃ vāto iṭṭho hoti kanto manāpo, evanti attho. Pānīyaṃva pipāsatoti pātumicchantassa pipāsato pipāsābhibhūtassa. Aṅgīrasīti aṅge rasmiyo assāti aṅgīrasī, tameva ārabbha ālapanto vadati. Dhammo arahatāmivāti arahantānaṃ navalokuttaradhammo viya.

"Like the wind to one who is sweating, you are dear" means: just as the wind is wished for, dear, and pleasing to those who are sweating, for the purpose of removing sweat, so it is. "Like water to one who is thirsty" means to one wishing to drink, who is thirsty, who is overcome by thirst. "O Aṅgīrasī" means she is Aṅgīrasī because there are rays on her limbs; addressing her, he speaks with reference to her. "Like the Dhamma to the Arahants" means like the nine supramundane Dhammas to the Arahants.

Jighacchatoti [V 2.0264] bhuñjitukāmassa khudābhibhūtassa. Jalantamiva vārināti yathā koci jalantaṃ jātavedaṃ udakakumbhena nibbāpeyya, evaṃ tava kāraṇā uppannaṃ mama kāmarāgapariḷāhaṃ nibbāpehīti vadati.

"To one who is hungry" means to one who desires to eat, who is overcome by hunger. "Like water to a fire" means: just as someone might extinguish a blazing fire with a pot of water, so he says, "Extinguish the torment of sensual passion that has arisen in me on account of you."

Yuttaṃ kiñjakkhareṇunāti padumakesarareṇunā yuttaṃ. Nāgo ghammābhitatto vāti ghammābhitattahatthī viya. Ogāhe te thanūdaranti yathā so nāgo pokkharaṇiṃ ogāhitvā pivitvā aggasoṇḍamattaṃ paññāyamānaṃ katvā nimuggo sukhaṃ sātaṃ vindati, evaṃ kadā nu kho te thanūdaraṃ thanavemajjhaṃ [P 3.0702] udarañca otaritvā ahaṃ sukhaṃ sātaṃ paṭilabhissāmīti vadati.

"Filled with the pollen of filaments" means filled with the pollen of lotus filaments. "Like an elephant scorched by the heat" means like an elephant scorched by the heat. "I would plunge into your breast and belly" means: just as that elephant, having plunged into a pond and drunk, finds pleasure and delight while submerged with only the tip of its trunk visible, so he says, "When, indeed, having plunged into your breast and belly—between your breasts and upon your belly—will I obtain pleasure and delight?"

“Accaṅkusova nāgova, jitaṃ me tuttatomaraṃ;

Kāraṇaṃ nappajānāmi, sammatto lakkhaṇūruyā”ti. –

"Like an elephant beyond the goad, the goad and spear have been conquered by me; I do not know the reason, intoxicated by her well-proportioned thighs."

Ettha tuttaṃ vuccati kaṇṇamūle vijjhanaayadaṇḍako. Tomaranti pādādīsu vijjhanadaṇḍatomaraṃ. Aṅkusoti matthake vijjhanakuṭilakaṇṭako. Yo ca nāgo pabhinnamatto accaṅkuso hoti, aṅkusaṃ atīto; aṅkusena vijjhiyamānopi vasaṃ na gacchati, so “jitaṃ mayā tuttatomaraṃ, yo ahaṃ aṅkusassapi vasaṃ na gacchāmī”ti madadappena kiñci kāraṇaṃ na bujjhati. Yathā so accaṅkuso nāgo “jitaṃ me tuttatomara”nti kiñci kāraṇaṃ nappajānāti, evaṃ ahampi lakkhaṇasampannaūrutāya lakkhaṇūruyā sammatto matto pamatto ummatto viya kiñci kāraṇaṃ nappajānāmīti vadati. Atha vā accaṅkusova nāgo ahampi sammatto lakkhaṇūruyā kiñci tato [M 2.0295] virāgakāraṇaṃ nappajānāmi. Kasmā? Yasmā tena nāgena viya jitaṃ me tuttatomaraṃ, na kassaci vadato vacanaṃ ādiyāmi.

Here, a `tutta` is called an iron rod for prodding at the base of the ear. A `tomara` is a spear-like rod for prodding at the feet and so on. An `aṅkusa` is a hooked thorn for prodding on the head. And whichever elephant is in rut and beyond the goad, has gone past the goad; even when being prodded with the goad, it does not come under control. That elephant, thinking, "The goad and spear have been conquered by me, since I do not come under the control of even the goad," does not understand any reason due to the pride of its rut. Just as that elephant beyond the goad, thinking "The goad and spear have been conquered by me," does not know any reason, so too, he says, "I, intoxicated, maddened, heedless, like one insane, by her who has well-proportioned thighs endowed with auspicious marks, do not know any reason." Alternatively: "Like an elephant beyond the goad, I too, intoxicated by her with well-proportioned thighs, do not know any reason for dispassion from her." Why? "Because, like that elephant, the goad and spear have been conquered by me; I do not accept the words of anyone who speaks."

Tayi gedhitacittosmīti bhadde lakkhaṇūru tayi baddhacittosmi. Gedhitacittoti vā gedhaṃ ajjhupetacitto. Cittaṃ vipariṇāmitanti pakatiṃ jahitvā ṭhitaṃ. Paṭigantuṃ na sakkomīti nivattituṃ na sakkomi. Vaṅkaghastova ambujoti baḷisaṃ gilitvā ṭhitamaccho viya. “Ghaso”tipi pāṭho, ayamevattho.

"My mind is greedy for you" means: Good lady with well-proportioned thighs, my mind is bound to you. Or, "a mind greedy" means a mind that has fallen into greed. "My mind is transformed" means it stands having abandoned its natural state. "I am not able to go back" means I am not able to turn back. "Like a fish that has swallowed a hook" means like a fish that stands having swallowed a hook. There is also the reading `ghaso`; this is the same meaning.

Vāmūrūti vāmākārena saṇṭhitaūru, kadalikkhandhasadisaūrūti vā attho. Sajāti āliṅga. Mandalocaneti itthiyo na tikhiṇaṃ nijjhāyanti mandaṃ ālocenti olokenti, tasmā [V 2.0265] “mandalocanā”ti vuccanti. Palissajāti sabbatobhāgena āliṅga. Etaṃ me abhipatthitanti etaṃ mayā abhiṇhaṃ patthitaṃ.

"O you with beautiful thighs" means one whose thighs are beautifully formed, or the meaning is one whose thighs are like the trunk of a banana tree. "Embrace" means embrace. "O you with gentle eyes" means: women do not stare sharply; they look and gaze gently. Therefore, they are called "gentle-eyed." "Embrace me" means embrace me completely. "This is my desire" means this has been constantly wished for by me.

Appako vata me santoti pakatiyāva mando samāno. Vellitakesiyāti kesā muñcitvā piṭṭhiyaṃ vissaṭṭhakāle sappo [P 3.0703] viya vellantā gacchantā assāti vellitakesī, tassā vellitakesiyā. Anekabhāvo samuppādīti anekavidho jāto. Anekabhāgoti vā pāṭho. Arahanteva dakkhiṇāti arahantamhi dinnadānaṃ viya nānappakārato pabhinno.

"Though my love was small" means being naturally slight. "By her with flowing hair" means: she is "one with flowing hair" because her hair, when unbound and let down upon her back, moves and ripples like a snake; by her, the one with flowing hair. "It has become manifold" means it has become of many kinds. Or, there is the reading `anekabhāgo` (of many parts). "Like an offering to an Arahant" means like a gift given to an Arahant, it has diversified in many ways.

Yaṃ me atthi kataṃ puññanti yaṃ mayā kataṃ puññamatthi. Arahantesu tādisūti tādilakkhaṇappattesu arahantesu. Tayā saddhiṃ vipaccatanti sabbaṃ tayā saddhimeva vipākaṃ detu.

"Whatever merit has been made by me" means whatever merit has been made by me. "In Arahants, such ones" means in Arahants who have attained the characteristic of 'suchness'. "May it ripen together with you" means may all of it give its result only together with you.

Ekodīti ekībhāvaṃ gato. Nipako satoti nepakkaṃ vuccati paññā, tāya samannāgatoti nipako. Satiyā samannāgatattā sato. Amataṃ muni jigīsānoti yathā so buddhamuni amataṃ nibbānaṃ jigīsati pariyesati, evaṃ taṃ ahaṃ sūriyavacchase jigīsāmi pariyesāmi. Yathā vā so amataṃ jigīsāno esanto gavesanto vicarati, evāhaṃ taṃ esanto gavesanto vicarāmītipi attho.

"Ekodī" means one who has attained singleness. "Nipako sato": "Nipaka" means one endowed with wisdom, which is called discernment. "Sato" means one endowed with mindfulness. "Amataṃ muni jigīsāno": Just as that Buddha-sage seeks and searches for the Deathless, Nibbāna, so too do I seek and search for you, O Sūriyavacchasā. Or, the meaning is: just as he wanders seeking and searching for the Deathless, so too do I wander seeking and searching for you.

Yathāpi muni nandeyya, patvā sambodhimuttamanti yathā buddhamuni bodhipallaṅke nisinno sabbaññutaññāṇaṃ patvā nandeyya toseyya. Evaṃ nandeyyanti [M 2.0296] evameva ahampi tayā missībhāvaṃ gato nandeyyaṃ, pītisomanassajāto bhaveyyanti vadati.

"Yathāpi muni nandeyya, patvā sambodhimuttamaṃ": Just as the Buddha-sage, seated on the Bodhi-seat, having attained omniscient knowledge, would rejoice and be pleased. "Evaṃ nandeyyaṃ": In the same way, I too, having become united with you, would rejoice, filled with joy and happiness—so he says.

Tāhaṃ bhadde vareyyāheti aheti āmantanaṃ, ahe bhadde sūriyavacchase, sakkena devānamindena “kiṃ dvīsu devalokesu devarajjaṃ gaṇhasi, suriyavacchasa”nti, evaṃ vare dinne devarajjaṃ pahāya “sūriyavacchasaṃ gaṇhāmī”ti evaṃ taṃ ahaṃ vareyyaṃ iccheyyaṃ gaṇheyyanti attho.

"'Tāhaṃ bhadde vareyyāhe'ti: 'Ahe' is a vocative particle, meaning 'O noble lady, O Sūriyavacchasā.' When Sakka, lord of the devas, offered the choice, saying: 'Will you take kingship in the two deva worlds, or Sūriyavacchasā?'—given such a choice, I would renounce divine kingship and say, 'I will take Sūriyavacchasā.' Thus, 'I would choose you, I would desire you, I would take you.' Such is the meaning.

Sālaṃva na ciraṃ phullanti tava pitu nagaradvāre naciraṃ pupphito sālo atthi. So ativiya manoharo. Taṃ naciraṃ phullasālaṃ viya. Pitaraṃ te sumedhaseti atisassirīkaṃ tava pitaraṃ vandamāno namassāmi namo karomi. Yassāsetādisī pajāti yassa āsi etādisī dhītā.

"'Sālaṃva na ciraṃ phullaṃ'ti: There is a sāla tree that has recently blossomed near your father's city gate. It is exceedingly delightful, like that recently blossomed sāla tree. 'Pitaraṃ te sumedhase'ti: I venerate and salute your exceedingly glorious father; I pay homage to him. 'Yassāse tādisī pajā'ti: He who had such a daughter.

349. Saṃsandatīti [V 2.0266] kasmā gītasaddassa ceva vīṇāsaddassa [P 3.0704] ca vaṇṇaṃ kathesi? Kiṃ tattha bhagavato sārāgo atthīti? Natthi. Chaḷaṅgupekkhāya upekkhako bhagavā etādisesu ṭhānesu, kevalaṃ iṭṭhāniṭṭhaṃ jānāti, na tattha rajjati. Vuttampi cetaṃ “saṃvijjati kho, āvuso, bhagavato cakkhu, passati bhagavā cakkhunā rūpaṃ, chandarāgo bhagavato natthi, suvimuttacitto bhagavā. Saṃvijjati kho, āvuso, bhagavato sota”ntiādi (saṃ. ni. 4.232). Sace pana vaṇṇaṃ na katheyya, pañcasikho “okāso me kato”ti na jāneyya. Atha sakko “bhagavatā pañcasikhassa okāso na kato”ti devatā gahetvā tatova paṭinivatteyya, tato mahājāniyo bhaveyya. Vaṇṇe pana kathite “kato bhagavatā pañcasikhassa okāso”ti devatāhi saddhiṃ upasaṅkamitvā pañhaṃ pucchitvā vissajjanāvasāne asītiyā devatāsahassehi saddhiṃ sotāpattiphale patiṭṭhahissatīti ñatvā vaṇṇaṃ kathesi.

349. "'Saṃsandatī'ti: Why did he praise the sound of the song and the sound of the lute? Does the Blessed One have any passionate attachment thereto? He does not. The Blessed One is equanimous with sixfold equanimity in such situations; he merely knows what is desirable and undesirable, but does not become attached to it. And this has been said: 'Friend, the Blessed One has the ear...' and so on. If, however, he had not spoken its praise, Pañcasikha would not have known, 'An opportunity has been granted to me.' Then Sakka, thinking this, would have turned back from there with the deities, which would have been a great loss. But knowing that when its praise was spoken, Pañcasikha would understand that an opportunity had been granted, approach with the deities, ask a question, and at the conclusion of the answer, be established in the fruit of stream-entry along with eighty thousand deities—knowing this, he spoke its praise.

Tattha kadā saṃyūḷhāti kadā ganthitā piṇḍitā. Tena kho panāhaṃ, bhante, samayenāti tena samayena tasmiṃ tumhākaṃ sambodhippattito paṭṭhāya aṭṭhame sattāhe. Bhaddā nāma sūriyavacchasāti nāmato bhaddā sarīrasampattiyā sūriyavacchasā. Bhaginīti vohāravacanametaṃ, devadhītāti attho. Parakāminīti paraṃ kāmeti abhikaṅkhati.

"Tattha kadā saṃyūḷhā": When were they entwined? That is, when were they tied and massed together? "Tena kho panāhaṃ, bhante, samayena": At that time, venerable sir, that is, in the eighth week from your attainment of supreme enlightenment. "Bhaddā nāma sūriyavacchasā": Bhaddā by name, and Sūriyavacchasā by virtue of her physical beauty. "Bhaginī": This is a term of address, meaning 'daughter of the devas'. "Parakāminī": She desires another, she yearns for him.

Upanaccantiyāti [M 2.0297] naccamānāya. Sā kira ekasmiṃ samaye cātumahārājikadevehi saddhiṃ sakkassa devarājassa naccaṃ dassanatthāya gatā, tasmiñca khaṇe sakko tathāgatassa aṭṭha yathābhucce guṇe payirudāhāsi. Evaṃ tasmiṃ divase gantvā naccantī assosi.
